text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. The most common type is supervised learning, where we give the computer a set of training data. This data includes examples with known answers, like photos labeled “cat” or “dog.” The computer studies these examples to build a model, which is essentially a mathematical rule that connects input to output. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For example, after training on many labeled photos, it can predict whether a new photo shows a cat or dog. We measure success by accuracy—how often the model’s predictions are correct. Better training data usually leads to higher accuracy.
